display.title: Episode 554: Naftali and the Three-Foot Chanukah Candles (Zos Chanukah)
display.summary_short: A Zos Chanukah show: every mitzvah is a light to be done with warmth, Shema with a four-year-old guest, and how a Rebbe's advice to buy very tall Chanukah candles saved a traveler from robbers.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Zos Chanukah, the eighth day of Chanukah 5753. Uncle Yossi teaches that 'a mitzvah is a candle and Torah is light': just as Hashem began Creation with light, every mitzvah brings light and warmth into a dark world, and the dancing flames of the menorah teach us to daven, learn and give tzedakah with liveliness and joy. A four-and-a-half-year-old boy and his mother lead the Shema, followed by tzedakah, Tehillim for the Rebbe's recovery and an advertisement. Story time: Naftali, who always danced on Chanukah, explains why. Before traveling home for Chanukah he asked his Rebbe for a blessing and was told to buy Chanukah candles three feet tall. Stranded by a blizzard, he was stopped by robbers who told him to say his last prayers. He climbed onto his wagon and lit all eight tall candles; fire watchmen on a distant tower saw the flames and galloped over, and the robbers fled. After another advertisement and a Zos Chanukah Hakochainik march, Uncle Yossi reads a letter from a girl whose teacher plays the programs in class.
display.lesson: Every mitzvah brings light into the world; do mitzvos with warmth and joy, like the dancing Chanukah flames.

date.note: 'Here we are enjoying the eighth day of Chanukah'; Zos Chanukah 5753 fell on Sunday 27 Dec 1992.
